src.label: 1972 Talisman, p. 272, Associated Students officer photograph; the caption reads "Above—Reginald Glass, vice president; Nancy Pape, secretary; Linda Jones, president; Joe Glasser, treasurer." Four officers stand round a pool table in the caption's left-to-right order, confirmed by the two named women holding the middle positions and by Glass, whom the same volume calls the body's first black vice president, at the left. Glasser is the rightmost figure, leaning across the table; the crop is of him, and other players at the tables behind remain in frame.

1973 Talisman, p. 416, the sophomore class page headed "Berman led sophs during a quiet year". Two figures are seated on a rock; the caption names them as the year's class officers and places vice-president Mike Inman at the left, leaving Berman as the figure at the right, which is the crop. The same volume's Sigma Alpha Epsilon chapter page separately lists Berman as ASG's sergeant-at-arms among its members' honours that year, and the volume's index carries one Louis Berman, on that chapter page and on this one.

1973 Talisman, p. 375, senior class portrait, "PATRICK D. LONG, Speech, Franklin, Ohio" — the only Patrick Long in the volume's index, cited there to pages 347 and 375. Page 347 names him president of the Young Democrats' club; the same volume's Associated Student Government feature (p. 74) separately names him co-head, with Gary Whitfield, of ASG's Legal Rights Committee. The Herald of 1 Sep 1972, reporting the vote that made him parliamentarian, describes him as a senior speech major from Franklin, Ohio, matching the caption on class, major and home town.

1977 Talisman, p. 350, senior portraits; "GERARD FAULK, JR., Elem. Ed., Bowling Green" is the second of five names in its block, matching the second of five portraits in that row, whose order runs man, man, woman, woman, man against Fatheddin, Faulk, Martha Ferguson, Nancy Ferralasco and Robert Fields. The volume's index carries one Gerard Faulk, Jr. That the senior of this name is the Judicial Council chairman rests on the name itself; no source found here puts Faulk's portrait and his ASG office on the same page.

1977 Talisman, p. 350, senior portraits; "GERARD FAULK, JR., Elem. Ed., Bowling Green" is the second of five names in its block, matching the second of five portraits in that row. 1978 Talisman, p. 372, senior portraits; "GARY W. REED, Accounting, Lexington" is the fourth of five names in its block, matching the fourth of five portraits in that row, whose order runs woman, man, woman, man, woman against Mari Rector, J.C. Redd, Connie Reece, Reed and Anita Reeves. The volume's index carries one Gary W. Reed, on this page and in the Accounting Club group photograph. That the accounting senior of this name is the treasurer the Herald reported elected in April 1977 rests on the name and the subject; the volume never names ASG's treasurer.

1978 Talisman, p. 383, junior class portraits; "PATRICIA COOK, Scottsville" is the sixth of nine names in its block, matching the sixth of nine portraits in that row. The volume's index reads "Cook, Patricia Ann 35, 383", and p. 35 is the page reporting the Herald editorial's joke day named for Cook as interim ASG secretary, so the yearbook itself ties the officer to this portrait.

1981 Talisman, p. 325, senior portraits; "STEVEN J. FULLER, history, Quality" is the sixth of six names in its block, matching the sixth of six portraits in that row. 1976 Talisman, p. 295, the Panhellenic Conference photograph, captioned "(Front row) Barb Osborn, Charlotte Gilliam, Jan Guy, Tricia Faith. (Second row) Nancy Crumb, Donna Filburn, Becky Bauer, Brenda Stafford, Charlotte Hiler, Sherry Casbier. (Back row) Mary Reeder, Chanda Davis, Susan Hurley, Debbie Rowe and Marilyn York." The photograph carries fifteen women in three groups of four, six and five, matching the caption's rows; five stand at the back in that order, Hurley is the third, and the crop is of her. That the woman pictured is the Associated Student Government officer rests on more than the name: the same volume enters Susan Louise Hurley at pp. 63, 268 and 295, p. 63 being ASG's own attendance roll and p. 268 the Chi Omega page, whose text names Hurley an ASG representative that year.

1979 Talisman, p. 344, the alphabetical senior portraits, captioned "DEBBIE ANDERSON, public relations, Bowling Green." One headshot per name in reading order, four rows of five; Anderson is fourth in her row, after Betsy A. Alspaugh, Ray Althaus and Cheryl Anderson and before John E. Anderson III, and the row's order runs woman, man, woman, woman, man against those names. The volume's index carries one Deborah Ann Anderson, at pp. 276 and 344. That the senior of this name is the Judicial Council member rests on the name itself; the 1979 volume has no student government section, and no source found here puts Anderson's portrait and her ASG post on the same page.

1979 Talisman, p. 364, senior class portraits. The caption reads "MELINDA MANIS, elem. ed., Marietta, Ga.", first of five names captioned for that row; the crop is the leftmost portrait in the row, matching her position as first-listed. The row's five captioned names run woman, woman, woman, man, woman against its five portraits, the man fourth in both, so the block's order is confirmed independently of the count. The volume's index carries one Melinda Susan Manis, at pp. 325 and 364; p. 325 is the Chi Omega group photograph, and the 1979 volume has no student government section. That the senior of this name is the Judicial Council alternate rests on the name itself, as with the Debbie Anderson portrait in this file.

Herald, 17 Feb 2023, photographed by Sean McInnis for "SGA Judicial Council unanimously votes against censure of President Bornefeld regarding use of social media"; the single figure pictured is captioned as the Student Government Association Speaker of the Senate, giving remarks at a judicial hearing in Downing Student Union on 17 February 2023. The two photograph captions spell the surname "Mischuck"; the article's own text spells it "Mishchuk" throughout, as this archive does, following SGA's own Senate minutes.

Back row: Jeffrey Sharp, Gary Dawson, Paul Deom, Steven Boehm"; Deom is third from left in the back row, immediately left of the figure in the patterned sweater. The article on the page names him as the junior from Boonville, Indiana who contacted the Louisville KCLU chapter over the university's dorm room inspection policy. The volume's index carries one Deom, Paul, at pp. 261, 266 and 282, and it is p. 261 that calls him an Associated Student Government member.

1987 Talisman, p. 343, sophomore class portrait, fourth row, third from left, "WILLIAM SCHILLING, Union", taken the year before his term as 1987-88 administrative vice president. The yearbook's index carries one Leneave, Christopher M., and refers him to p. 303 and to pp. 114 and 116, where he is named in the Associated Student Government group photograph and in the second government photograph; the index entry is what ties the class portrait to the ASG committee chairman.

The caption belonging to the photograph is printed in the caption block on the facing page, p. 109, and describes the cluttered desk and the telephone call before naming him: "Nation serves as administrative vice-president of Associated Student Government." The same spread carries president Jeff Consolo's list of his fellow officers, which names Paul Nation administrative vice-president.
